title: Antitrust Storm Sweeps the Tech Industry: U.S. Department of Justice Strongly Advances Injunctions, Firefox Faces Survival Crisis

content_html:
The highly anticipated Google antitrust case has reached a critical turning point, as the U.S. Department of Justice is working hard to prevent Google from paying large fees to major browsers to maintain its default search engine status. However, this strict measure, intended to break Google's industry monopoly, has unexpectedly placed Mozilla, the parent company of Firefox browser, in an unprecedented survival crisis.

As the absolute leader in the search engine market, Google spends over $26 billion annually on securing default search engine positions. Although the court previously rejected the request to completely ban such payments, the Department of Justice maintains in its appeal that Google is using its monopoly funds to stifle future emerging competitors.

The vital source of revenue faces a cutoff, independent browser vendors are in dire straits

For Mozilla, which heavily relies on this funding, the Department of Justice's payment ban is a disaster. According to statistics, about 85% of Mozilla's revenue in the U.S. market comes directly from Google's default position payments. Once this funding is lost, its business operations will be difficult to sustain.

In previous submissions, Mozilla had already publicly warned that banning default payments would force independent developers to completely exit the browser and engine market. Now, as the ban progresses further, this pessimistic prediction is gradually becoming a very dangerous reality.

Irony under regulatory dilemma, Google to submit response in September

This antitrust battle is full of dramatic and ironic elements. The ban may not effectively weaken Google's control, but it could directly kill its remaining independent competitors. In this legal battle that determines their survival, browser vendors like Mozilla have even been restricted in their right to speak out.

According to the legal procedure, Google will submit its formal response brief on September 29. Faced with this fate-changing legal storm, independent browser vendors who rely entirely on Google's payments can only hope that Google's defense will be successful.

content_html_zh:
备受期待的谷歌反垄断案已经到了关键的转折点，美国司法部正在努力阻止谷歌向各大浏览器支付大笔费用以维持其默认搜索引擎地位。 然而，这一旨在打破谷歌行业垄断的严厉措施，却意外地让火狐浏览器母公司Mozilla陷入了前所未有的生存危机。

作为搜索引擎市场的绝对领导者，Google 每年花费超过 260 亿美元来确保默认搜索引擎地位。 尽管法院此前驳回了完全禁止此类支付的请求，但司法部在上诉中坚称谷歌正在利用其垄断资金来扼杀未来新兴竞争对手。

重要收入来源面临断流，独立浏览器厂商陷入困境

对于严重依赖这笔资金的 Mozilla 来说，司法部的付款禁令是一场灾难。 据统计，Mozilla 在美国市场约 85% 的收入直接来自于 Google 的默认仓位支付。 一旦失去这笔资金，其业务运营将难以维持。

在此前提交的文件中，Mozilla 已公开警告称，禁止违约付款将迫使独立开发者彻底退出浏览器和引擎市场。 现在，随着禁令的进一步推进，这种悲观的预测正在逐渐变成非常危险的现实。

讽刺监管困境下谷歌将于9月提交回应

这场反垄断之战充满了戏剧性和讽刺性的成分。 该禁令可能不会有效削弱谷歌的控制力，但可能会直接杀死其剩余的独立竞争对手。 在这场决定生存的法律战中，Mozilla等浏览器厂商的发言权甚至受到限制。

根据法律程序，谷歌将于9月29日提交正式回应简报。 面对这场改变命运的法律风暴，完全依赖谷歌支付的独立浏览器厂商只能寄希望于谷歌的辩护能够成功。
